model: Xi / MXi gas water heaters (ETH-1000 / Mirius gateway)
applies_to: A. O. Smith commercial gas water heaters with Xi 1.0 or MXi controls (such as Cyclone) fitted with the ICC ETH-1000 or Mirius communication gateway.
summary: A. O. Smith's Xi and MXi gas water heater controls talk to BACnet through an ICC gateway: the Mirius gives BACnet MS/TP and the ETH-1000 gives BACnet IP. Each heater appears as a virtual BACnet device with tank temperatures, setpoint and differential, run-time and fault counters, safety-switch inputs, relay states and state/fault/alert codes. The BMS can write the setpoint and use an EMS control word to enable or disable heating.
firmware: Mirius V3.300, ETH-1000 V4.002 (device object values in the manual)
notes: The manual says not all models support all objects and some names differ by model; a column marks which points apply to Xi 1.0 and which to MXi controls.
Temperatures are in °C on the bus; the setpoint limits are also given in °F.

The manual's R/W column is blank for BI 312-320, the BO relay states (described as commanded relay status), the BVs and the multistate values; access for those rows is not given, and they are listed here as read-only.

AV 263 EMS Mode-Status uses coded values: Xi 1.0 writes 3841 to enter EMS mode, 1/0 to enable/disable heating, 3584 to refresh and 3840 to leave; MXi writes 32769 (enable heating), 32768 (disable) or 0 (no EMS control).
The table refers to state and fault tables by numbers that do not match the printed tables; the states here come from the CCB state table (Table 11) and the fault table (Table 14).
The gas table prints no objects at AV 203-206 (the electric table uses them for bank differentials).

source.title: Installation Manual: Inter-Appliance Communications, Communication Node for EMS/BMS Control (ETH-1000 / Mirius)

integration.summary: Install the ICC gateway (Mirius for BACnet MS/TP, ETH-1000 for BACnet IP) on the heater and set its address and device instance with ICC Configuration Studio. The BMS writes the tank setpoint (AV 201) and, if it should switch heating, takes EMS control through AV 263, which then has to be refreshed at least every 30 s. Read the tank temperature, CCB state and fault/alert codes.

minimum_points.name: System State
minimum_points.why: CCB state: standby, purge, heating, fault

integration.enable: Heating on/off from the BMS goes through AV 263 EMS Mode-Status. Xi 1.0: write 3841 to enter EMS mode, then 1 to enable or 0 to disable heating; write 3840 to leave EMS mode. MXi: write 32769 to enter EMS mode with heating enabled, 32768 for EMS mode with heating disabled, 0 for no EMS control. Heating still also depends on tank temperature falling below setpoint minus differential and on the external thermostat if that option is on.
integration.heartbeat: Xi 1.0: write 3584 (EMS Mode Refresh) within 30 s, 15 s or less recommended, or EMS mode ends and the heater resumes normal operation. MXi: the enable-heating command must be resent at least every 30 s or heating is disabled. On MXi software below 3.16 EMS mode cannot be cleared over BACnet; only a power cycle clears it.
setup: Gateway settings (address, baud, device instance, device name, IP) are changed with the ICC Configuration Studio software over USB.
Mirius defaults: Modbus address 1, BACnet MS/TP MAC 81, device instance 520081 for gas models.
MS/TP baud rates listed: 4800-115200; the ETH-1000 uses DHCP by default and supports foreign-device registration.
Device object defaults: name Water Heater-01, vendor ICC, Inc. (242).
gotchas: The EMS word reads back with bit 14 set (0xC000/0xC001); a brief 0x8000 reading is normal between refreshes.
After leaving EMS mode with 3840 on Xi 1.0, write 0 and 3584 to clear leftover bits 1 and 14.
Some objects are Xi 1.0 only or MXi only; check which control the heater has.
Temperatures are in °C even where the setpoint range is quoted in °F.
